turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I am not acting out of fear of the Mussulmans, Sandip. I am acting out of a sense of responsibility to my people and my land. Your actions have consequences, and I will not stand idly by while you threaten my tenants.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Oh, Nikhil, you are as melodramatic as ever. Your sense of responsibility is as thin as your poetry. Your tenants, I dare say, are better off with me, for I have fire in my belly, unlike the tepid waters you offer them.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: I feel caught between you both, Sandip, Nikhil. Your words are like fire and ice, each trying to convince me of your righteousness.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: My dear Nikhil, your tenants are the fortunate ones to be under my wing. I bring them the light of progress and revolution, not the shadows of your outdated ideals. Your fear is misplaced, as always.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your so-called progress is but a mask for your tyranny, Sandip. My tenants may not see it now, but they will suffer under your rule. I warn you again, cease your oppressive ways.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Nikhil, your warnings are like the distant rumble of thunder on a sunny day. I know your heart is heavy with the fear of change, but change is inevitable, my dear opponent. Your tenants will see the dawn of a new era, not the shadows of your cowardice.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your words are but empty promises, Sandip. I have seen the destruction your rhetoric brings, and I will not stand idly by.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Oh, Nikhil, you are like a moth circling the flame of progress, yet too afraid to feel its warmth. Your tenants will see the light, and your shadows will fade into insignificance.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I have seen the flame of progress, Sandip, and it burns with a fury that consumes all in its path. My tenants will not be your puppets in this charade of change.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Ah, Nikhil, your words are as melodramatic as ever. But tell me, do you not see the shackles you wear, bound by the chains of your own cowardice? My tenants will embrace the dawn, and your warnings will be but the whispers of the night.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your tenants see through your false promises, Sandip. They know the truth of your intentions and the danger you pose.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: And what truth, pray tell, do they see? The truth of a man who speaks of freedom yet is afraid to embrace it? My intentions, my dear Nikhil, are as clear as the rising sun, and the danger I pose is but a shadow in your delusions.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your intentions may be clear to you, Sandip, but they are a facade to your tenants. They will soon realize the reality of your oppressive rule.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: And what reality, dear Nikhil, do you speak of? The reality of a man who clings to the past, to the shadows of an empire long gone? My tenants will see the light, and your reality will fade into the dust of history.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your words are empty, Sandip. The reality your tenants will see is the oppression you bring, not the freedom you claim.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Your reality is but a narrow vision, Nikhil. My tenants will see the dawn of a new era, not the twilight of oppression. Your words are as hollow as the promises of those who came before.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: My tenants will not be fooled by your rhetoric, Sandip. They see through your false promises and fear the consequences of your rule.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Fear is but a fleeting shadow, Nikhil. My tenants will embrace the sunrise of freedom and prosperity, not the dark clouds of your outdated fears. My promises, unlike those of the past, are rooted in the soil of truth and progress.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your promises are but hot air, Sandip. The truth lies in the suffering of my tenants under your rule. The progress you claim is nothing more than a facade.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Your tenants, Nikhil, see through the fog of your complacency. They yearn for the sun that I promise to bring. My words are the seeds of freedom, not the barren soil of your inaction.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I say, Nikhil, don't you keep Browning among your books here? I was just telling Queen Bee of our college club. Do you remember that contest of ours over the translation of those lines from Browning? You don't?

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I managed to get together the words to render it into Bengali, somehow, but the result was hardly likely to be a 'joy forever' to the people of Bengal. I really did think at one time that I was on the verge of becoming a poet, but Providence was kind enough to save me from that disaster. Do you remember old Dakshina? If he had not become a Salt Inspector, he would have been a poet. I remember his rendering to this day ... No, Queen Bee, it is no use rummaging those bookshelves. Nikhil has ceased to read poetry since his marriage--perhaps he has no further need for it. But I suppose 'the fever fit of poesy', as the Sanskrit has it, is about to attack me again.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I have come to give you a warning, Sandip

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: About the fever fit of poesy?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: For some time, Mahomedan preachers have been about stirring up the local Mussulmans. They are all wild with you, and may attack you any moment.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Are you come to advise flight?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I have come to give you information, not to offer advice.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Had these estates been mine, such a warning would have been necessary for the preachers, not for me. If, instead of trying to frighten me, you give them a taste of your intimidation, that would be worthier both of you and me. Do you know that your weakness is weakening your neighbouring zamindars also?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I did not offer you my advice, Sandip. I wish you, too, would refrain from giving me yours. Besides, it is useless. And there is another thing I want to tell you. You and your followers have been secretly worrying and oppressing my tenantry. I cannot allow that any longer. So I must ask you to leave my territory.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: For fear of the Mussulmans, or is there any other fear you have to threaten me with?
